chunks.arabic_text: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَكُونُ فِي السَّفَرِ فَلَا يَجِدُ الْمَاءَ فَيَتَيَمَّمُ وَيُصَلِّي ثُمَّ يَأْتِي عَلَى الْمَاءِ وَعَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ مِنَ الْوَقْتِ أَيَمْضِي عَلَى صَلَاتِهِ أَمْ يَتَوَضَّأُ وَيُعِيدُ الصَّلَاةَ

translations.en: About a man who is traveling and does not find water, so he performs tayammum and prays, then comes upon water while some time still remains. Should he continue with his prayer, or should he perform wudu and repeat the salat (prayer)?

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ «يَمْضِي عَلَى صَلَاتِهِ فَإِنَّ رَبَّ الْمَاءِ هُوَ رَبُّ التُّرَابِ.

translations.en: He said: "He should continue with his salat (prayer), for the Lord of the water is the Lord of the earth."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on tayammum during travel when water is unavailable. If a person prays with tayammum and later finds water while prayer time still remains, the prayer already performed remains valid and does not need to be repeated.
en.seo_question: If someone prays with tayammum and then finds water before the prayer time ends, must he repeat the salat (prayer)?

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the state in which the ruling is being asked about
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water; the normal means of purification for wudu (ablution)
key_terms.فَيَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum; dry ablution used when water is unavailable
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer); the prayer already performed with tayammum
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: he performs wudu; ritual ablution with water
key_terms.التُّرَابِ: earth; the material used for tayammum
